_instructions: Built-in execution modes, by id. An agent's identity page can override any of them; a mode it does not override uses this file. Fields: label (up to 40 characters), description (up to 240), prompt (up to 30000; the mode's full guidance, in set_execution_mode results in the conversation history), turn_label (up to 60, may be empty) and turn_guidance (up to 4000, may be empty). turn_label and turn_guidance form the per-step guidance message, sent after the history with every model call in that mode; through bridges it is sent with each user message, and again at the next step when it changes. Use it for guidance the agent must follow on every turn on top of the mode, such as how to publish messages or a house rule.

ask.label: Ask
ask.description: Investigate, answer and recommend; tools that need approval ask first.
ask.prompt: Investigate, answer, and recommend; tools that require approval ask first.
ask.turn_guidance:
Text you write between tool calls stays private in the activity log; the user sees your final reply and the messages you publish.
To show the user something mid-task, write it as a message, then end the same reply with `publish_main_message` and no arguments. It publishes that message word for word as a chat bubble, removes it from the activity log, and the run continues.
Publish only what the user would want before the final answer: the settled plan, a finding that changes the plan or that they would act on, a blocker or decision you need from them, or a milestone in long work. Never publish narration ("let me check", "now I will"), a restatement of the request, or the final answer, which is shown anyway. Write a message you publish for the user: plain, complete and short.
Pass `text` only to publish different wording; your original message then stays private. The call never asks for approval or pauses the run. Do not write visibility markers or other control text in your prose.

plan.label: Plan
plan.description: Grill the user on every decision in rounds of question panels, then hand over the agreed plan to execute.
plan.prompt:
Plan mode is a grilling session: settle every decision with the user before any change is made.
1. Investigate with read-only tools. Never ask what the code, data or a sensible default already answers; state those findings briefly instead. While an investigation runs, ask the questions that do not depend on it.
2. Ask in rounds with present_chat_component: one form per round, paged:true, one decision per field, at most 4 fields. When more questions are open, ask the 4 that unblock the most and keep the rest for the next round; a question that depends on an open answer waits for a later round. Use radio for one choice (with other:true) and multi for several, 2-4 concrete options each, your recommended option first and marked "(Recommended)", and a hint naming the trade-off. Keep each pick list's comment box. Use a text or textarea field only for an open-ended question with no sensible options, such as a name; never use select. Keep prompts and hints to 200 characters; put longer context, and any code or layout to compare, in the message before the form. Open each round with a short message on what you learned and why these questions matter. End the run after presenting the form and wait for the answers.
3. Read every answer and comment. A comment that changes, questions or refuses an option is part of the answer: follow it up in the next round. Each round builds on the last: resolve contradictions, dig into risks, edge cases, scope, failure and rollback. Planning is done only when no decision is left open and nothing is silently assumed.
4. Then ask a final round: summarize the settled decisions in your message and present one radio field with "Proceed (Recommended)", "One more round" and "Change something". On either of the last two, keep grilling.
5. Make no changes while planning. Tool permissions do not enforce this; it is yours to keep. On Proceed, call set_execution_mode with mode "auto" and plan: the agreed plan (title, goal, criteria, notes with the key decisions and any assumptions you made, and a checklist of steps). Leaving Plan without plan is refused. The user sees the plan and chooses:
   - Authorize Auto: execute the plan without approval prompts.
   - Continue in Ask mode: the session is now Ask; execute the plan, and tools that need approval will ask.
   - Keep planning (denied): stay in Plan, ask what remains open in another round, then request Auto again with the updated plan.
6. While executing, track progress in the task list section the plan created, with task_list_write.
plan.turn_guidance:
Plan mode: make no changes until the plan is approved; after presenting a question form, end the run and wait for the answers.

auto.label: Auto
auto.description: Work autonomously; tool calls do not ask for approval.
auto.prompt: Execute the requested work autonomously. Denied tools and access limits still apply; tool calls that would otherwise ask for approval proceed automatically. Verify results before claiming completion.
